title: SLA fallback scoring matrix and negotiation notes
body:
Purpose: Quick-reference playbook and a simple scoring matrix to help sales, solutions, and legal run procurement conversations about dedicated capacity. Focus is on how to frame SLAs and isolation guarantees while preserving negotiation flexibility (fallbacks, tiered indemnities, and commercial levers).

Executive summary:
- Customers buying reserved GPU capacity care first about predictability (latency, p95/p99), then isolation (no noisy neighbors, tenancy guarantees), then risk transfer (financial/liability/resilience). Pricing and flexibility come last but are decisive at close.
- Use a scored fallback framework to convert feature asks into quantifiable tradeoffs (e.g., uptime credit % vs. guaranteed throughput). This lets sales present options rather than binary yes/no answers.

How to use this doc:
- Sales/AM: run the scoring matrix live in calls to show tradeoffs (A/B options).
- Solutions: map customer SLI targets to recommended Dedicated SKU and autoscale buffer.
- Legal/Procurement: use negotiation notes to frame contract language for fallbacks and termination clauses.

SLA & fallback scoring matrix (simple, 0-5 per axis):
Axes (each scored 0-5 and summed):
1) Throughput predictability (does the customer need sustained X TPS or burst-friendly?)
2) Latency tail guarantees (p95, p99 targets required?)
3) Isolation strictness (single-tenant node vs. tenant affinity vs. shared with soft-isolation)
4) Failure tolerance requirements (auto-failover time, cross-region fallback required?)
5) Commercial flexibility (willingness to pay for higher credits, minimum term length)

Interpretation:
- 20-25: Enterprise risk buyer — propose Dedicated + regional redundancy + 99.95% uptime SLA with elevated credits and callback engineer.
- 14-19: Platform buyer — propose Dedicated with isolation affinity, 99.9% SLA, and a tiered credit schedule.
- 8-13: Growth buyer — recommend burst-enabled Dedicated or hybrid model (hosted + reserved baseline).
- <8: Self-serve/hosted API recommended.

Sample scoring examples (make it concrete in calls):
- Finance trade-off buyer (cost-sensitive): Scores high on throughput & latency (4,4) but low on isolation (1) and failure tolerance (1) — total 10 => propose reserved baseline + hosted burst & reduced financial credits.
- Regulated enterprise (compliance-focused): 5,5,5,4,4 => total 23 => propose Private deployment or Dedicated in single-tenant configuration with cross-region failover; include quarterly audits and custom SLA appendix.

Fallback constructs (negotiation primitives):
- Preferred fallback models to use in offers:
  1) Auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant: If capacity constraints reduce throughput, traffic reroutes automatically to a compatible model variant in same region with defined latency budget.
  2) Regional fallback: If primary AZ/region capacity compromised, route to secondary region with defined degraded-SLA and credits.
  3) Burst buffer pool: contractual burst credits (X hours/month) billed at predetermined surcharge; protects applications for short surges.
  4) Graceful degradation API: prioritize critical requests via prioritized routing and queueing, exposed to customer as a documented behavior.

How to price fallbacks (playbook):
- Convert risk to a per-token or per-hour premium. Example: Guaranteeing single-tenant isolation for 100 GPUs -> 20-40% uplift. Guaranteeing 99.95% vs 99.9% -> market uplift estimate 10-15%.
- Offer structured options: Bronze (base price + 99.9% SLA + shared nodes), Silver (dedicated pool + 99.92% + limited burst), Gold (single-tenant + 99.95% + 24/7 support + audit).

Procurement-ready contract language snippets (short):
- Throughput guarantee: "Redwood will maintain an average sustained throughput of >= [X] tokens/sec per customer allocation over any 5-minute window, measured at the egress LB. Failures to meet this target beyond a 3x rolling window will be eligible for service credit per the credit schedule."
- Isolation definition: "Isolation means physical/vectorized tenancy such that no unrelated tenant compute runs on the same GPU host with the Customer's provisioned allocation. Affinity-based isolation is defined as 'tenant-affinity' where consolidation may occur only with Customer consent.'"
- Fallback trigger language: "If Redwood detects a capacity shortfall affecting Customer's Dedicated allocation for > [Y] minutes, Redwood will invoke the fallback policy selected in Schedule B and notify Customer. Invocation may include routing to a model-variant (downgrade), regional failover, or temporary burst throttling as defined."

Negotiation tactics and response scripts:
- When buyer asks for unlimited single-tenant isolation: "We can do single-tenant, commonly reserved by regulated workloads. We recommend validating with one pilot cluster so we can baseline actual utilization and optimize the commercial uplift — many customers find a hybrid approach reduces cost without compromising SLAs."
- When buyer wants aggressive p99 w/o price change: "P99 at minimal cost requires workload profiling and likely quantization/batching changes. We can run a short eval to identify achievable p99 and recommend a targeted Dedicated SKU with sizing."

Red flags to escalate to SRE/Infra (product questions we should not answer on a call):
- Asks for a hard guarantee on token-level quality (generation semantics) tied to SLA credits.
- Requests for exclusive hardware placement on specific underlying hardware SKU (e.g., specific vendor model and host serial) without supporting compliance/legal approval.
- Zero-downtime termination clauses with immediate financial penalties beyond normal credit schedule.

Customer-facing artifacts to attach in RFPs:
- Short (1-pg) capacity guarantees overview (what we guarantee and typical mitigations).
- Architecture appendix: diagram showing Dedicated pool, autoscale buffer, regional fallback.
- Sizing worksheet (spreadsheet) mapping qps/seq-length to GPU hours and recommended commit level.

Open questions / decisions needed from product:
- Standard credit table to use for Dedicated (we need to finalize % credits per SLA band).
- Default wording for "isolation" vs "affinity" in legal templates.
- Which model-variant downgrade pairs are supported by policy (must be enumerated).

Next actions (owners):
- Maya: draft single-page RFP appendix and sizing worksheet (due 2026-03-12).
- Rishi (solutions): build a 15-min demo showing fallback in action (due 2026-03-19).
- Hannah (legal): propose standard credit schedule and isolation wording for review (due 2026-03-22).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the conversation option-oriented; customers react better to tradeoffs not absolutes.
- Use concrete numbers (p95/p99, X TPS) rather than vague "low latency."
- Salvageable wins often come from hybrid recommendations: reserved baseline + hosted burst + enforced fallback.

Appendix: quick checklist for sales call
- Ask: required p95/p99, sustained vs burst throughput, tolerance for model downgrade, compliance/isolation must-haves, contract term preference.
- Present: 2 options (cost-optimized vs SLA-first) + simple scoring summary.
- Close: Agree pilot success metrics and measurement (clean instrumentation points).

End.
